correctness.rationale: For any inscribed ball, the \(n\) lower coordinate clearances together with the rank-facet clearance give the sharp global bound \(r/(n+\sqrt n)\). When that bound exceeds \(1/2\), opposite coordinate facets give the sharper universal cap \(1/2\). The displayed centers attain the corresponding bounds, and equality forces every coordinate of the center, proving uniqueness. For the outer sphere, uniqueness and full coordinate-permutation symmetry force a scalar center \(t\mathbf1\). The squared distance to a vertex of cardinality \(k\) is exactly \(nt^2+k(1-2t)\), so the farthest layer and its minimizer are determined by the sign of \(1-2t\), yielding the threshold \(2r=n\) and the stated contact sets.

value.rationale: Uniform-matroid independence polytopes are canonical objects in matroid and Ehrhart geometry, and the primary source singles them out as a basic application. The theorem gives a complete Euclidean inner/outer radius profile, unique centers, and contact phases throughout the entire family. The value is structural rather than a single closed form: the inball and minimum-enclosing sphere saturate at two different rank thresholds, revealing a separation between facet-controlled and vertex-layer-controlled geometry.
